title: Meta claims billions in IRS tax credits for experimental AI data centers
source_used: ET Datacenters summary of the New York Times report of 30 Sep 2026
key_facts: Meta classes its AI data centers as experimental projects to claim the US Research and Experimentation Tax Credit, per the New York Times.
Meta's tax bill was cut by 2 billion dollars in 2024 and it expects to save 3.9 billion in 2025, up from 700 million in 2023 before the credit was used for data centers.
In its tax filings Meta describes its AI data centers as 'pilot models'; Meta declined to say what makes them experimental.
Some Meta finance staff doubted the strategy would withstand scrutiny; the IRS has previously rejected claims for proven, commercially available equipment.
Meta's unrecognized tax benefits rose 45 percent to 18.74 billion dollars from 12.9 billion.
Meta spokesman Andy Stone said Meta invested 200 billion dollars in R&D over five years and uses incentives Congress set for domestic investment.
James Shannon, the former congressman who sponsored the credit, said Meta's use goes 'way, way beyond' what anyone imagined.
quote_evidence: In its tax filings, Meta describes its multibillion-dollar AI data centers as "pilot models."

why_it_matters_hint: Taxpayers and lawmakers may ask why AI data centers earn a research tax break.
